title: need to somehow back-off subtype checks in strategy options to suit the selectin_polymorphic() subclass load case

labels.name: loader options
labels.description: ORM options like joinedload(), load_only(), these are complicated and have a lot of issues

labels.name: inheritance
labels.description: issues to do wtih ORM inheritance, a particularly tricky area

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
we document this pattern:

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/queryguide/inheritance.html#combining-additional-loader-options-with-selectin-polymorphic-subclass-loads

```py
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectin_polymorphic
stmt = (
    select(Employee)
    .order_by(Employee.id)
    .options(
        selectin_polymorphic(Employee, [Manager, Engineer]),
        selectinload(Manager.paperwork),
    )
)
objects = session.scalars(stmt).all()
print(objects[0])
print(objects[0].paperwork)
```

What's awkward there is we are allowing `selectinload(Manager.paperwork)` to exist in a query that's against `Employee`.

Trying to do this for any kind of pathing obviously fails:

```py
stmt = select(Company).options(
    selectinload(Company.employees).options(
            selectin_polymorphic(Employee, [Manager]),
            selectinload(Manager.paperwork)
    ),

)

```

and

```py
stmt = select(Company).options(
    selectinload(Company.employees).selectin_polymorphic(Employee, [Manager]),
    selectinload(Company.employees).selectinload(Manager.paperwork)
)

```

with, as expected:

```
sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: ORM mapped entity or attribute "Manager.paperwork" does not link from relationship "Company.employees".  Did you mean to use "Company.employees.of_type(Manager)"?

```

that's an important error.  We need to raise that, that's a major path people need to know about.  However, it means our documented pattern is broken.        

The pattern works perfectly fine if I take out the error checks:

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
index d59fbb7693..0f2f7c3c63 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
@@ -1116,10 +1116,10 @@ class Load(_AbstractLoad):
 
         assert cloned.propagate_to_loaders == self.propagate_to_loaders
 
-        if not orm_util._entity_corresponds_to_use_path_impl(
-            cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", parent.path[-1]),
-            cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", cloned.path[0]),
-        ):
+        if False: #not orm_util._entity_corresponds_to_use_path_impl(
+            #cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", parent.path[-1]),
+            #cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", cloned.path[0]),
+        #):
             if len(cloned.path) > 1:
                 attrname = cloned.path[1]
                 parent_entity = cloned.path[0]
@@ -1731,10 +1731,10 @@ class _LoadElement(
         assert cloned.local_opts == self.local_opts
         assert cloned.is_class_strategy == self.is_class_strategy
 
-        if not orm_util._entity_corresponds_to_use_path_impl(
-            cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", parent.path[-1]),
-            cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", cloned.path[0]),
-        ):
+        if False: #not orm_util._entity_corresponds_to_use_path_impl(
+            #cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", parent.path[-1]),
+            #cast("_InternalEntityType[Any]", cloned.path[0]),
+        #):
             raise sa_exc.ArgumentError(
                 f'Attribute "{cloned.path[1]}" does not link '
                 f'from element "{parent.path[-1]}".'
@@ -1854,9 +1854,9 @@ class _AttributeStrategyLoad(_LoadElement):
             assert False
 
         # here we assume we have user-passed InstrumentedAttribute
-        if not orm_util._entity_corresponds_to_use_path_impl(
-            path[-1], attr.parent
-        ):
+        if False: #not orm_util._entity_corresponds_to_use_path_impl(
+            #path[-1], attr.parent
+        #):
             if raiseerr:
                 if attr_group and attr is not attr_group[0]:
                     raise sa_exc.ArgumentError(

```


so not sure what to do here, if we somehow could test that the selectin_polymorphic() option was actually set already, which would be extremely difficult to achieve.

full test

```py
from typing import List

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, select
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, joinedload, with_polymorphic, defaultload
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from sqlalchemy.orm import mapped_column
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectin_polymorphic
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Company(Base):
    __tablename__ = "company"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str]
    employees: Mapped[List["Employee"]] = relationship(
        back_populates="company"
    )


class Employee(Base):
    __tablename__ = "employee"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str]
    type: Mapped[str]
    company_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("company.id"))
    company: Mapped[Company] = relationship(back_populates="employees")

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"{self.__class__.__name__}({self.name!r})"

    __mapper_args__ = {
        "polymorphic_identity": "employee",
        "polymorphic_on": "type",
    }


class Manager(Employee):
    __tablename__ = "manager"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("employee.id"), primary_key=True
    )
    manager_name: Mapped[str]
    paperwork: Mapped[List["Paperwork"]] = relationship()
    __mapper_args__ = {
        "polymorphic_identity": "manager",
    }


class Paperwork(Base):
    __tablename__ = "paperwork"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    manager_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("manager.id"))
    document_name: Mapped[str]

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Paperwork({self.document_name!r})"


class Engineer(Employee):
    __tablename__ = "engineer"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("employee.id"), primary_key=True
    )
    engineer_info: Mapped[str]
    __mapper_args__ = {
        "polymorphic_identity": "engineer",
    }


engine = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

conn = engine.connect()
session = Session(conn)
session.add(
    Company(
        name="Krusty Krab",
        employees=[
            Manager(
                name="Mr. Krabs",
                manager_name="Eugene H. Krabs",
                paperwork=[
                    Paperwork(document_name="Secret Recipes"),
                    Paperwork(document_name="Krabby Patty Orders"),
                ],
            ),
            Engineer(name="SpongeBob", engineer_info="Krabby Patty Master"),
            Engineer(
                name="Squidward",
                engineer_info="Senior Customer Engagement Engineer",
            ),
        ],
    )
)
session.commit()

stmt = select(Company).options(
    selectinload(Company.employees).options(
            selectin_polymorphic(Employee, [Manager]),
            selectinload(Manager.paperwork)
    ),

)

# or

stmt = select(Company).options(
    selectinload(Company.employees).selectin_polymorphic([Manager]),
    selectinload(Company.employees).selectinload(Manager.paperwork)

)

objects = session.scalars(stmt).all()



print(objects[0].employees[0])
print(objects[0].employees[0].paperwork)

```
